description: The Wood Rooster in Chinese astrology: personality, Wood element traits, 1945 and 2005 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Wood Rooster is the Rooster born in a Wood year, one of five versions of the tenth animal. It combines the Rooster's precision with Wood's qualities. Wood Rooster years between 1924 and 2044 are 1945 and 2005. The Rooster's fixed element is Metal.

sections.heading: The Wood Rooster personality
paragraphs: A Rooster born under Wood meets a softer material than its own nature. The Rooster's fixed element is Metal, and Metal controls Wood, so the animal is said to carve and trim its year stem, shaping Wood's generous growth with its own precision. In practice, Wood Roosters are pictured as conscientious idealists: honest, hardworking and eager to improve the systems around them, yet warmer and more cooperative than many of their sign. They like to organise community efforts and fix what is broken. The carving dynamic gives them clarity, but it can turn critical, and readings note that Wood Roosters may hold themselves and others to standards that leave little room for ordinary human mess.

In the five-element scheme, Wood belongs to the east and to the green energy of early spring, and that seasonal image shapes how it colours an animal sign. A Wood stem tends to soften sharp edges and add warmth, curiosity and a cooperative instinct. Traditional texts associate it with benevolence, growth and the wish to build something that lasts beyond the self. People born under a Wood stem are often portrayed as principled, open-handed and hopeful about others. The caution usually attached to Wood is a habit of spreading energy thinly, saying yes to every request and feeling quietly hurt when generosity is not returned in kind.

sections.heading: Wood Rooster at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, the Wood element is usually linked with planning, teaching and collaborative building. Wood-year people are often described as good at seeing how a team could grow and at nurturing the people inside it, which suits roles in education, design, community work, healthcare and any field with a long horizon. They tend to prefer cooperation over rivalry. The traditional warning is about scope: a Wood stem can start more ventures than it can finish, so firm priorities and honest deadlines usually serve it well.

Organised and idealistic, the Wood Rooster likes to make systems fairer as well as tidier. Public administration, teaching, editing, event planning and charity governance are often suggested, as precision and social conscience combine in each. It needs clear goals, a team willing to keep standards high and acknowledgement of the effort it pours into detail. In love, the Wood Rooster is loyal, attentive and generous with practical help, from proofreading a partner's application to planning a holiday down to the train times. It wants appreciation and shared values. Friction comes from its exacting eye: it may notice every small flaw in shared plans and point them out before praising anything.

sections.heading: Wood Rooster years and dates
paragraphs: Between 1924 and 2044 the Wood Rooster years are 1945 (February 13, 1945 to February 1, 1946) and 2005 (February 9, 2005 to January 28, 2006). Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1945 anyone born before Feb 13 is a Wood Monkey, not a Wood Rooster. The combination returns every sixty years, since five elements cycle through twelve animals and only meet the same pairing again after five rounds of the zodiac. Every Wood Rooster year is Yin, matching the Rooster's own polarity.

Chinese almanacs call the combination Yi-You, joining the heavenly stem Yi to the earthly branch You. Births just before each new year fall in the Wood Monkey year (before February 13, 1945) and the Wood Monkey year (before February 9, 2005), and births in the weeks after each Wood Rooster year ends belong to the Fire Dog. The new year itself fell on a Tuesday in 1945 and Wednesday in 2005.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Wood Rooster
paragraphs: Patience with imperfection is the gift Wood Roosters most often need to give, starting with themselves. Before correcting a colleague or partner, asking whether the issue truly matters can save goodwill. Their reforming energy works best when invited, so offering suggestions rather than verdicts tends to land better. Wood Roosters often thrive in roles where organisation serves people directly: running events, teaching, managing volunteers. Gardening suits them unusually well, combining tidiness with patience for slow growth. Accepting help without redoing it afterwards builds trust. When precision and kindness walk together, Wood Roosters make communities run beautifully.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Wood Rooster shares the Rooster's San He trine with the Ox and Snake (the Metal trine), its Liu He bond with the Dragon, and its Liu Chong clash with the Rabbit. The element adds a second layer: another Wood sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Wood in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Wood Rooster years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1945 (from February 13, 1945) and 2005 (from February 9, 2005). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Wood Rooster's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Wood and the Rooster's fixed element is Metal; in the five-element cycles metal controls Wood. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Wood Rooster?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Ox and Snake (San He) and the Dragon (Liu He). The Rabbit is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Wood Rooster called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Yi-You. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Wood stem Yi, followed by its earthly branch, here You for the Rooster, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Wood Rooster different from other Roosters?
faq.answer: All Roosters share precision, candour and diligence. The Wood year element changes the tone: wood is the element of spring and of things that grow, so a Wood year is traditionally said to lend any animal a generous, expansive streak.
